Joe Brady's football intelligence
stories.summary:
There was some discussion in the training camp thread for today about Joe Brady's press conference, and about how he seems to be doing a little better in presenting his thoughts orally.  Earlier in the year, people reacted to his machine-gun style of talking. I did, too. It makes him sound like he isn't smart. Whenever I think that, I remember having heard someone tell a story about Brady and his football brilliance. 



	 



	Today I asked Gemini to tell me that story.  Maybe everyone has heard it. If so, I apologize. Here it is:



	
		Quote
	

	
		
			 
		

		
			That story centers on a pivotal moment early in Joe Brady’s career while he was a young graduate assistant at Penn State under offensive coordinator Joe Moorhead.
		

		
			 
		

		
			When & Where It Happened
		

		
			 
		

		
			In early 2017, Moorhead took his Penn State offensive staff to New Orleans for a professional development visit with Sean Payton and the New Orleans Saints coaching staff. The trip took place at the Saints’ facility in Metairie, Louisiana.
		

		
			 
		

		
			The Key People Involved
		

		
			 
		

		
			Joe Brady: Then a 27-year-old graduate assistant at Penn State, working largely behind the scenes on film breakdown and opponent analysis.
		

		
			Joe Moorhead: Penn State’s offensive coordinator, who brought his staff to exchange ideas with the Saints.
		

		
			Sean Payton: Saints Head Coach, known for running one of the most sophisticated offensive systems in the NFL.
		

		
			Pete Carmichael Jr.: Saints Offensive Coordinator.
		

		
			 
		

		
			What Happened in the Meeting
		

		
			 
		

		
			Moorhead had introduced a highly successful RPO (run-pass option) and hurry-up spread scheme at Penn State. Payton invited the staff down to study those college concepts, expecting a high-level exchange with Moorhead.
		

		
			 
		

		
			During the chalk talk, the Saints coaches began asking granular, technical questions about specific defensive reads, coverage adjustments, and how the offense handled niche blitz packages. Moorhead handed the whiteboard marker over to Brady, who knew the precise micro-details of the system inside and out.
		

		
			 
		

		
			Brady took over the presentation, walking the Saints staff through the exact mechanics, film clips, and logic of the system. He detailed how defenders' body language dictated options and explained technical wrinkles that Payton’s staff had not seen mapped out with that level of precision.
		

		
			 
		

		
			The Impressions Formed
		

		
			 
		

		
			The Saints staff were stunned by Brady’s mastery, composure, and technical intelligence for someone of his age and role.
		

		
			 
		

		
			Immediate Respect: Sean Payton and Pete Carmichael were so blown away by the "kid graduate assistant" that Payton immediately kept Brady on his radar.
		

		
			 
		

		
			The Job Offer: Shortly after that meeting, Payton hired Brady as an offensive assistant for the Saints in 2017. Brady spent two years in New Orleans absorbing Payton's offensive principles—an experience that directly launched him to LSU in 2019 (where he won the Broderick Award and a national championship) and eventually back to the NFL.
		

		
			 
		

		
			The Narrative: Moorhead later joked in interviews that he went to New Orleans to give a presentation and ended up losing his best assistant because Brady blew everyone in the room away.
		

		
			 
		
	



	 



	 



	The way I heard the story, maybe it was Carmichael who told it, was that while Brady was running the meeting, people on the Saints staff who weren't in the meeting heard some kid was knocking it out of the park, so they joined the meeting. It was by all accounts a stunning performance



	 



	The guy knows football.

stories.title: The Athletic QB Tiers (2 Panelists Voted Josh as Tier 2)
stories.summary:
The annual Athletic QB Tiers came out this morning.  Unbelievably, 2 panelists voted Josh as a tier 2 QB!  These 2 panelists must be incredibly spiteful or astonishingly stupid.  How do you not immediately dismiss any contributors to your story that claim Allen is not in the top tier of QBs in the NFL?!  I know it is a paywall article, but here is the link.  https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/interactive/nfl-quarterback-tiers-insider-rankings-2026/ 



	 



	How panelists voted in 2026



	Tier 1  - 48 votes



	Tier 2 - 2



	 



	Allen moved one vote closer toward unanimous Tier 1 status and could be the most feared quarterback in the league.



	“Josh Allen is unreal,” a defensive coordinator said. “He and Stafford are the two guys I would not want to play the most. Allen’s ability to make plays, be hard to tackle, put the team on his shoulders — when it’s fourth down, he is going to win.”



	 



	One veteran coach said Allen still has much to learn.



	“Josh Allen, with under 30 seconds left in the half, runs for a meaningless 12-yard gain and fumbles and gives up a field goal in a playoff game to go behind two scores against Denver,” this coach said. “Until he quits doing that, you can’t rank him as the top quarterback. That is one of the worst plays I’ve ever seen. Cost them the game.”



	 



	Others saw the positives.



	“The thing that jumped out to me about the playoffs last year was the physicality and the plays the quarterbacks make with their toughness, their size and their strength, particularly as they advance on,” an exec said. “Josh has got that. Obviously, it’s TBD with (new coach) Joe Brady, but one thing that those guys in the top tier do is, when you get off the bus on the road, the other 52 guys think they got a chance.”



	Allen led all quarterbacks in rushing yards (579) and rushing touchdowns (14) in 2025.



	 



	“He’s the real deal because he can do it as a dropback quarterback, and they do some run game with him,” another defensive coordinator said. “The way they use him is the way Baltimore has to use Lamar (Jackson) to get the most out of him.”



	A GM noted that the Bills have given Allen a strong defense and a strong run game, but not at the same time.



	“Josh is a 1 because he is the reason they remain competitive,” this GM said. “He’s so physically talented. But I’m ready to say he’s never gonna win a Super Bowl because their team’s getting worse around him, and I think his style of football is going to start breaking him down physically.”

stories.title: CJGJ = Problem Child?
stories.summary:
As many of you have, I have been tuned into the offseason/Training Camp and I have to be honest, I am seeing something brewing that makes me feel uneasy.  It's CJ Gardner-Johnson.  When they first signed him, I was like ok, they got a dawg style guy with some talent.  Hey we need some dawgs and this could help our defense.  However, after seeing the constant sh***t talking and now this whole streaming "thing" with Brady and then going live after to talk about it.  It's clear to me this guy just doesn't get it.  Almost like some Antonio Brown vibes.  He has had issues with his former teams.  Quite a few teams I might add. 



	 



	There was a certain culture developed here over the past 8-9 years. You heard Jim Leonhard reference it in his presser regarding the level of professionalism that is displayed by the players.  I fully understand if it gets out of control they can just cut him, but I hope this guy doesn't kill the vibes and make training camp unenjoyable for everyone. This can have a ripple effect throughout the team.  He appears to be the exact type of player (attitude and maturity) we have tried to avoid over the last 9 years.
